newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk govt MP says prime minister change no problem.
newsitem.headline: Turk govt MP says prime minister change no problem.

text.p: A leading Turkish Islamist deputy said on Friday he saw no problem with the handover of the prime minister's post to deputy coalition leader Tansu Ciller next week to solve the shaky government's dispute with the military.

"Yes, I can say at the moment there is no problem related to that," Welfare's Salih Kapusuz told a news conference when asked if Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan would hand over power to conservative Ciller by June 18.
Erbakan announced earlier this month that the 11-month-old coalition would seek early elections and that Ciller would lead a caretaker government into early polls.
The Islamist-led government suffered another series of body blows on Friday, pushing it closer to collapse after months of political gridlock.
A secularist cabinet member resigned, citing what he said were government Islamist leanings at odds with Turkey's decades-old tradition of keeping party politics out of the mosque.
And a far-right powerbroker refused a government invitation to form a broader coalition to ward off an anti-Islamist campaign by the secularist army.
